intro: Your duty of care is the legal responsibility to keep people safe and well while respecting their rights and choices.
points: Your duty of care applies automatically the moment you begin caring; you cannot opt out of keeping people safe.
Work only within your training and competence, and never attempt tasks you have not been trained to do.
Balance safety with rights: support positive risk-taking, as a person with capacity may make choices you consider unwise.
Report incidents, errors and near misses honestly; near misses are early warnings that let you prevent future harm.
Under the duty of candour, be open when something goes wrong and apologise sincerely — covering up is worse.
Keep professional boundaries, decline personal gifts, and speak up about safeguarding concerns — you are protected when whistleblowing genuinely.
